story.title: Serbia just elected the world's brainiest parliament

draft:
The most credentialed legislature on record just took seats in Belgrade.

Serbia’s new parliament is composed of more than 70% members holding PhDs or equivalent research credentials—far above any other national assembly. The surge stems from a recent electoral law that rewards academic achievements, turning academia into a political springboard.

I’m intrigued by what this means for tech policy. On one hand, deep scientific literacy could accelerate evidence‑based legislation on AI, data privacy, and research funding. On the other, a homogenous elite may overlook practical constraints faced by startups and workers on the ground. The real test will be whether these scholars can translate theory into policies that balance innovation with societal impact.

Will we start seeing more countries experiment with “brainpower quotas” as a model for governance, or will the experiment expose the limits of expertise without broader representation?
